body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Análises.
**Pronúncia:** Expressividade.
**22 palavras novas** (análises).
**Texto do dia:** charge, tirinha e cartum.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo integrar leitura, escuta, fala e escrita sobre uma charge de análise e debater suas ideias com estruturas da unidade.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: The Graph That Went Up

bubbles: Impressive. How do you account for it?
We sold one unit last year, and three this year.
A figure whose size depends on where you start.
Had you told me the base, I would not have printed the headline.
If the graph were smaller, it would have been more honest.

blocks.say: Say what the cartoon criticises about statistics.

items.q: The analyst says that sales rose by 300%.
The boss accepts the claim without question.
items.why: How do you account for it?

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
rows: **Had you told me**, I would not have printed it.
**If the graph were smaller**, it **would have been** honest.

blocks.body: Para analisar uma charge: **o que mostra → o que critica → como (humor, exagero) → por quê**. Use as estruturas da unidade para dar precisão.

items.s: How do you ___ for the increase? (account)
A figure ___ size depends on the start. (whose)
___ you told me, I would not have printed it. (Had)
If the graph ___ smaller, it would have been honest. (be, were)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: What should the analyst have said
items.pt: O que o analista deveria ter dito?

body: **Lies, damned lies and statistics** — Mentiras, mentiras cabeludas e estatísticas
**Cherry-pick the data** — Escolher só os dados convenientes
**Spin the numbers** — Manipular os números
**Take at face value** — Aceitar pelo valor aparente
**Moving the goalposts** — Mudar as regras
**Read the small print** — Ler as letras miúdas
**Smoke and mirrors** — Fumaça e espelhos
**Call someone’s bluff** — Desafiar o blefe de alguém
**What does the cartoon criticise?** — O que a charge critica?
**What should the analyst have said?** — O que o analista deveria ter dito?
**Misleading statistics: a figure whose size depends on the base.** — Estatísticas enganosas: um número cujo tamanho depende da base.

blocks.title: Group debate
lines: Misleading statistics: a figure whose size depends on the base.
Estatísticas enganosas: um número cujo tamanho depende da base.
What should the analyst have said?
O que o analista deveria ter dito?
Had he given the base, nobody would have been misled.
Se tivesse dado a base, ninguém teria sido enganado.

items.label: Expressividade
items.note: Organização da informação pela entonação: a informação nova ou final recebe a nota que cai; listas e ideias incompletas sobem.
words: We need time ↗, money ↗, and trust ↘.
If it fails ↗, we try again ↘.
Having left early ↗, she missed it ↘.

prompts.model: Had he given the base, nobody would have been misled.
Honest charts, whose scales are clear, build trust.

blocks.task: Write a 7-sentence review of the cartoon, with at least four structures from the unit.
blocks.model: The cartoon criticises misleading statistics. The analyst announces a 300% rise, a figure whose size depends entirely on a tiny base. The boss asks how he accounts for it. Had the analyst given the base, nobody would have been misled. If the graph were smaller, it would have been more honest. Critics single out percentages as the easiest way to mislead. On balance, the cartoon is sharp and fair.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
